summary: All three acceptance lines pass at PR #1086 head 232dc82f0f546e237d91a274ec014265a789d7e9 (code head 8c7a1d1f plus the implement handoff; the test file at the tip is byte-identical to the code head's). The dispatch-tools test passes from the repository root with the Dispatch variables unset, the whole plugin suite is green (61 pass across 7 files), the expected tool names come from dispatchToolSpecs and every one of the fourteen required-argument entries matches the contract, and the pull request's own envoy-plugin job runs a green `Test envoy plugin` step between Typecheck and Pack. No production code changed. The implementer's proof reproduced in full.

Every observation matched what implement.json states.

observations: The pane exports DISPATCH_URL and DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE (not DISPATCH_TOKEN); the spec's acceptance 1 requires them unset, so every local run used `env -u DISPATCH_URL -u DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE -u DISPATCH_TOKEN` and the scrub was confirmed from inside the scrubbed environment before the first run. The test also sets and restores its own DISPATCH_URL/DISPATCH_TOKEN, so it would pass either way; the scrub is the spec's condition, recorded here once.
Local bun is 1.3.14, the CI runner's is 1.4.2; both report the same counts (1 pass / 32 expects for the file, 61 pass / 137 expects for the suite).

For the tester, `jj restore` on the test file is safe (the change is committed in @-, so restore would return the committed content), but the revert was still done by hand per the plan's instruction and confirmed with a diff against 232dc82f.
The workflow's display name is `Legion Envoy and Contracts`; the spec calls it "Envoy and contracts". Same workflow file (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml).

`legion gh` reads were run from /tmp: from inside the workspace, gh's local-repository discovery hits the colocated worktree's stale .git pointer (implement.json trickyParts); with --repo explicit no local repository is needed.
